1 dng-compare: a manual for comparing and preserving DNG archives

A DNG can change without its sensor samples changing. Lightroom or another editor may write new XMP, update a preview, change a rating, or reorganize TIFF metadata. Whole-file checksums then differ, even when the photograph’s stored raw samples remain identical. Conversely, a matching filename, file size or stored digest is not enough to establish that two copies contain the same image.

This project separates those questions. It reads actual image blocks, decodes when the Python comparison needs to resolve different encodings, reports metadata differences, and can preserve an exact older file version as a complete original or a verified delta. Python coordinates the work. Rust supplies a bounded no-decoding scan and native workers. OCaml supplies alternative native metadata and byte workers with the same orchestration contract.

The public source is firstpair/dng-compare. The README gives the overview and the HOWTO gives a short path through a comparison. This manual describes what each verdict proves, what it leaves open, and how to reproduce the workflow without a personal photo library.
